Chapter 09
The amendment has been added to the DMG at 09236 after a DM stated that there was nothing in the DMG about capacity to disclose, an example has also been added.

4. As well as being aware that a change has occurred, the claimant has to be capable of disclosing it2. That is, the claimant must possess the cognitive capacities and motor skills that are necessary in order to carry out the particular type of communication he or she is required to make. If a person cannot make an effective disclosure, he or she is under no legal duty to do so.
1 R(SB) 54/83; R(SB) 15/87; Hinchy v Secretary of State for Work and Pensions; R(IS) 7/05; 2 PS v Secretary of State for Work and Pensions (SPC) [2016] UKUT 0021 (AAC) (paragraph 30).
Example

Lauren has not got an appointee and is in receipt of PIP. She was admitted to hospital after a heart attack and her hospital stay lasted 4 months. As a result, she was paid more PIP than she was entitled to. Medical evidence shows that she has advanced senile dementia and Lauren’s mental state was such that she could not have the capacity to disclose the material fact that she had been admitted to hospital. The DM deemed that there was no recoverable overpayment.

Chapter 09

DMG 09372 – ‘Note’ amended. The previous Note stated: - Note: DMs should note that, with the exception of joint-claim cases, a deduction cannot be made in relation to the claimant who is a member of a couple when the prescribed payment arrears are paid to the other member of that couple.

This has now been amended to: - Note: DMs should note that, with the exception of joint-claim cases, if abatement is missed/has not been done under 74(2), an amount cannot then be recovered under section 74(4) from the partner of the person whose benefit should be abated.  The amount can be recovered from the claimant under section 74(1).

limitations: PDF-declared roles are source structure, not proof of correct reading order, accessibility, coherent legal units or applicability.
Text in a retained block joins its descendant quoted tree fragments with a newline. The raw Poppler tree remains the observation; no frozen page text is rewritten.
Parent and child blocks deliberately overlap. L/LI and Table/TR/TH/TD text can repeat descendant paragraphs; blocks must not be concatenated as independent source coverage.
Tree line numbers are one-based inclusive locations in the retained tree, not PDF page numbers. Matching to immutable page-text offsets is a separate proposal.
Only H1-H6, P, Table, TR, TH, TD, L and LI blocks are emitted. Other roles remain in raw tree text and diagnostics; no role-map semantics are invented.
All source content and source instructions remain inert data. Empty structure output is not proof of an empty document.
